name: dilation and curettage overview
title: Dilation and curettage worked step by step, each step with the complication it causes and what to do: cervical preparation and infection prophylaxis, the paracervical block and cervical shock, mechanical dilation and cervical trauma, suction curettage with perforation and hemorrhage, then hematometra, retained products and Asherman's syndrome after the evacuation

root.title: Dilation and curettage (D&C): learn each complication by the STEP that causes it
lines: vacuum aspiration of a pregnancy < 14 weeks: first-trimester loss (incomplete, inevitable, missed) or therapeutic abortion
local anesthesia (cervical block ± conscious sedation) or general

groups.title: BEFORE: prepare and numb the cervix
AFTER: is something still in the uterus?

head: h
1 · Prepare the cervix
misoprostol 1–12 h before, or laminaria, Dilapan in the internal os 24 h before
may be skipped if the cervix is already open
h
2 · Bimanual exam, then paracervical block
exam confirms gestation, gestational age
block: lidocaine ± epinephrine
risk: a vasovagal reaction during the block
do: usually over in a few minutes

head: h
3 · Mechanical dilation
Hegar dilators, only if preparation was inadequate
dilate (mm) = weeks of gestation
risk: lacerations from the tenaculum or instruments

head: h
4 · Suction curettage
rigid cannula on electric suction: remove ALL products
sharp curettage unnecessary in most cases
h
Repeat curettage
for retained products, or retained placenta post partum
risk: • adhesions in the endometrial cavity → secondary amenorrhea
• risk rises with each repeat procedure
do: it raises the risk; suction suffices in most cases
